question.problem:
Let $⟨x,y,z⟩$ be the unique solution of the system of equations below. 

$$
{\begin{aligned}4x+y=-3 \\ x-3y-2z=4 \\ -2x+y+2z=-5\end{aligned}
$$

Given that the determinant of the coefficient matrix is equal to $-14,$ then $z=$
question.worked_solution:
First, let's rewrite the system to reveal the coefficients:

$$
{\begin{aligned}4x+1y+0z=-3 \\ 1x+(-3)y+(-2)z=4 \\ (-2)x+1y+2z=-5.\end{aligned}
$$

We start by writing the determinant of the coefficients matrix, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}D=|\begin{aligned}4 & 1 & 0 \\ 1 & -3 & -2 \\ -2 & 1 & 2\end{aligned}|=-14.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, to find ${D}_{z}$, we replace the third column by the right-hand side of the system, and calculate the determinant:

$$
\begin{aligned}{D}_{z}=|\begin{aligned}4 & 1 & -3 \\ 1 & -3 & 4 \\ -2 & 1 & -5\end{aligned}| & =4\cdot |\begin{aligned}-3 & 4 \\ 1 & -5\end{aligned}|-1\cdot |\begin{aligned}1 & 4 \\ -2 & -5\end{aligned}|+(-3)\cdot |\begin{aligned}1 & -3 \\ -2 & 1\end{aligned}| \\  & =4(15-4)-(-5+8)-3(1-6) \\  & =44-3+15 \\  & =56.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, applying Cramer's rule, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}z & =\frac{{D}_{z}}{D}=\frac{56}{-14}=-4.\end{aligned}
$$
